rows.subject: protocol message type "block"
rows.notes: M21.1: the client asks not to hear a player, naming them by the PlayerID that rides every chat line and every roster row — a display name would not do, since names are neither unique nor claimed. `blocked` is explicit rather than a toggle, so the two ends cannot disagree about which way to flip, and the same message lifts a block. The target's account (which decides durability) is resolved server-side across every hosted world, never trusted from the request; self and id-0 targets are refused at the write.

rows.subject: protocol message type "blockResult"
rows.notes: M21.1: the blocker's own confirmation, and the only message either party gets — the blocked player is never told, because a block that announces itself invites the retaliation it exists to prevent. `durable` says whether the block outlives the session (it cannot when the target is a guest: there is no id to key it on), and the server writes the displayed line because the server is what knows which of the four outcomes happened.

rows.subject: protocol message type "boardChange"
rows.notes: M16.8's pass.scn/main.scn (and most M16.4-M16.6 hub-to-feature-board scenarios) exercise the same underlying resync (RoomManager.Snapshot after a board change) WorldInstance.Tick wraps as a BoardChangeMessage; the wire struct itself is pre-existing WS-level coverage.

rows.subject: protocol message type "challengeError"
rows.notes: M32.1: an honest refusal on the challenge path — an unlisted id, an unavailable or player-owned world, a run that has ended or belongs to somebody else, or a server with recording switched off.

rows.subject: protocol message type "challengeResult"
rows.notes: M32.1: the server's own verdict on a run it observed complete — deterministic tick count and in-sim counters, whether the result became a durable row, and its rank. It is never requested by a client and carries no account id.

rows.subject: protocol message type "moderate"
rows.notes: M21.2: an operator asking for mute, unmute, kick or refuse. It names its target by the PlayerID that rides every chat line and every roster row, like block, and states the action rather than toggling one, so the two ends cannot disagree about which way to flip. Authority is never taken from the request: the server re-checks the ZZT_MODERATOR_ACCOUNTS allowlist on every message, so the snapshot's `operator` flag decides only what the window OFFERS. An unknown action is dropped, self-targeting is refused, and the whole message is rate-limited on chat's policy so the audit's denial path cannot be used to write to the operator's own record.

rows.subject: protocol message type "moderateResult"
rows.notes: M21.2: the operator's own confirmation, and only the operator's. `durable` is the honest limit made visible — a refusal binds to an accountID, so refusing a guest kicks them and nothing more, and a guest's mute ends with their connection — and the server writes the displayed line because the server is what knows which outcome happened. A denied action (not on the allowlist, self-targeting, or a target who has already left) comes back as `applied: false` with an explanation rather than as silence or an error.

rows.subject: protocol message type "moderationNotice"
rows.notes: M21.2: what the moderated PLAYER is told, and the one message in the M21 family addressed to the person acted upon — a block is silent by design, a sanction announces itself, or a player whose lines vanish learns only that the game is broken. `ended` marks the sanctions that finish the session (kick, refuse, and a refused account's rejected reconnect at the door), and the client has to honour it: without that the reconnect backoff walks a kicked player back in half a second later, presenting the resume token that reclaims the run they were removed from.

rows.subject: protocol message type "privateMessage"
rows.notes: M25.1: the client sends `privateMessage` with a live target PlayerID and text; the server-authored delivery fills sender and recipient presentation names and live ids. The sender receives an outgoing copy as confirmation, the recipient receives the incoming copy, and a third socket is fenced to prove it receives no PM frame. Account ids never appear in the message.

rows.subject: protocol message type "privateMessageResult"
rows.notes: M25.1: the sender's generic refusal for a PM that cannot be delivered. It covers a target who left, a recipient block, and the shared chat/PM rate limit; the blocked recipient is not notified, preserving M21.1's silent-block boundary.

rows.subject: protocol message type "profileRequest"
rows.notes: M24.1: the browser asks for a public profile by current PlayerID, never by display name or account id. The server resolves the live player, maps to the account privately, and the test asserts the request returns Ada's profile without exposing google:ada.

rows.subject: protocol message type "profileResult"
rows.notes: M24.1: the profile reply carries only the public window lines plus the claimed handle; account ids stay server-only. The test marshals the reply and fails if the target account id appears anywhere on the wire.

rows.subject: protocol message type "quitReply"
rows.notes: M16.8's prompt.scn drives a quit reply through RoomManager.SubmitQuitReply; the wire QuitReplyMessage struct itself is pre-existing WS-level coverage.

rows.subject: protocol message type "replayError"
rows.notes: M22.3: a recording whose named world is no longer hosted fails as an ordinary replay load error instead of panicking or joining a room. The WebSocket branch writes replayError before closing; the unit test pins the not-hosted failure at the loader seam.

rows.notes: Pre-existing WS-level coverage (M4.3a); M16.8 did not need to add to it.

rows.subject: protocol message type "snapshot"
rows.notes: M16.8: RoomManager.Snapshot's full-board dump is checked against the diff-only reconstruction at every checkpoint (full-snapshot-fallback-vs-diff-only convergence) and, over the wire, against the direct Engine's authoritative screen. M21.4 (2026-08-05): the join/resume snapshot gained `blockedPlayers`, which names which of the same message's `players` the recipient has already blocked — set only on the first frame of a connection, like `resumeToken`, and omitted entirely when the answer is empty. It carries PlayerIDs only: the durable half of a block is keyed on the target's accountID, so the answer is computed per visible player rather than shipped from the stored list, which would hand the recipient account ids they have no other way to see. The client merges it and never assigns from it, since a roster-scoped list can add knowledge and must not be able to withdraw any.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/gazette/edition
rows.notes: M34.2: the day written up. GET only; serves the cached edition (the author's if one was bought, the server's own otherwise) and kicks a bounded single-flight refresh, so a request never waits on a model. Names are substituted at read time from stored actor tokens; no account key and no token is marshaled.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/generate
rows.notes: M16.17: the route's whole answer matrix — a premise that generates, hosts and persists; GET of an unknown job 404; a method that is neither GET nor POST 405; a malformed or over-16KiB body 400; an empty or over-8000-byte premise 422; retry of an unknown job 404 and of a job with no resume state 409; the per-client pace 429; an unconfigured server 503 — plus the async job, its progress and its retry driven through the shipped binary. A refused request is proven to cost no model call. The `name` field is client-supplied and passes only through SanitizeSaveName: the destructive collision it allowed was filed as M16.17b and LANDED 2026-07-31 — the matrix now also covers a generation aimed at a world people are playing, which answers 409, paints no board and leaves the occupied world's bytes alone. M18.11 adds a third 409 subject: a premise aimed at a canonical Museum world (ErrGeneratedWorldIsCanonical), refused before the first board is painted and costing no model call. Only a name the player TYPED reaches that 409 — since M16.17d a plan-derived collision resolves to a minted name instead of failing.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/health
rows.notes: Scaling observability: the subprocess server exposes liveness and aggregate load counts at /api/health, and the test decodes an ok response with at least one hosted instance. M18.20 adds build identity to the same public summary: commit plus short stamp, without leaking M18.19's protected memory, instance, replay or editor detail.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/help
rows.notes: M16.16: a .HLP file by basename, 400 for a path/extension outside the contract, 404 for a missing file

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/highscores
rows.notes: M16.16: the vanilla heading and score lines; 400 for an unsafe world name

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/loadworld
rows.notes: M16.15: 200 naming the hosted world, 400 for a traversing name.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/metrics
rows.notes: Scaling observability: the subprocess server exposes /api/metrics with instance detail plus runtime memory and goroutine counters for production load runs.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/moderation/audit
rows.notes: M21.6: the operator console's read of the in-memory audit tail, oldest first, with the tail size reported alongside so a complete record is distinguishable from a truncated one (the file is the record); ?limit=N is the last N and a mistyped limit shows the whole tail rather than nothing; any method but GET is 405. A guest, a signed-in non-operator, an operator against an empty allowlist and a server with no auth service each get 404 rather than 403 — the console must not confirm it exists, and must not tell a non-operator there is an allowlist they are not on.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/moderation/refusals
rows.notes: M21.6: lists the standing refusals M21.2 imposes, each carrying who imposed it, when and in which world, oldest first with ties broken by account so two reads agree; the Account field is filled from the map key, because the document is hand-editable by design (Refuses tests membership, not the field) and a row that cannot be named cannot be lifted. Operator-gated on the same ZZT_MODERATOR_ACCOUNTS allowlist as the socket actions, 404 to everyone else, and any method but GET is 405.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/moderation/refusals/lift
rows.notes: M21.6: the hole M21.2 left — POST {"account"} lifts a refusal in the running process, and the account rejoins over a socket immediately afterwards (proved with a snapshot, not against the store). The lift reaches the document too, so the next restart does not re-impose it, and a failed write puts the entry back rather than leaving the process and the file disagreeing. Audited before the operator is told, carrying the refusal's own world and who imposed it; an account with no standing refusal is an audited no-op rather than an error (two operators reaching for the same row is normal), an empty account is 400, any method but POST is 405, and a denial is logged but never audited — this route is behind no rate limiter, so an audit a stranger could append to at will is one nobody can read.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/museum/play
rows.notes: M16.16: choices then selection then host and join, twelve refusal rows that create no cache entry / .ZZT / instance, 405 on GET and 400 on a junk body

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/museum/search
rows.notes: M16.16: the four-field fan-out and its dedup, the year field for a 4-digit query, an empty query that never leaves the process, no-match, 502 when the Museum is down, 405 on POST

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/preferences
rows.notes: M19.3: the account-wide preferences store's read/write route — a guest GET answers {authenticated:false} rather than failing, a guest PUT is 401 and writes nothing, PUT then GET round-trips the color, a junk color is sanitized to the vanilla player before it is stored, a malformed or oversized body is 400, any other method is 405; an explicitly stored empty color beats a stale browser pick at the next join. M21.1: BlockedAccounts is the store's second field — the second caller it was shaped for, added as a field rather than a store. M24.1: Profile is the next field; the route keeps read-modify-writing, refuses guest profile writes, normalizes a claimed handle, returns 409 on handle conflict, and preserves Color/Hints while saving profile.

rows.subject: HTTP/WS route /api/restore

rows.subject: Editor mode (browser editor UI)
rows.notes: M16.13 found three divergences from EditorLoop and M16.13a closed them: the session now installs InitElementsEditor's editor-only overrides (ForceDarknessOff, and E_INVISIBLE's 0xB0 glyph) on the Engine rather than the shared ElementDefs, so a dark board is edited lit and an invisible wall can be seen while a room ticking beside it keeps the game table; "Switch boards" lists board 0 under its own name (titleScreenIsNone false) while the exit and passage pickers still say "None"; and editorModified is raised on every accepted edit/board-info/stat reply, so leaving offers to save. The rest of editor mode is exercised by TestM1613BrowserEditorAndPortableOutput.

The browser golden "identity-paused-player-one" drives two real browsers onto one board and requires the pause overlay to mark only the viewer's own square; the M16.12 boundary tests require every per-player diff's roster and HUD to describe its own recipient, including across the stat-id reindexing a departure causes. Presentation addition with no vanilla counterpart.

rows.subject: Mobile on-screen keyboard for text surfaces
rows.notes: M16.18: all six editable modal kinds (modalAcceptsTextInput) certified on Chromium and WebKit touch profiles at portrait/landscape and DPR 3 — mount, gesture activation, IME composition, deletion, and no leak of a play-mode key to the wire — plus the same surfaces on Chromium/Firefox/WebKit desktop, where no native control mounts at all.

rows.subject: Mobile touch movement/shoot/torch/pause controls
rows.notes: M16.18a (2026-08-01) shipped the controls the owner chose on 2026-07-15 to build rather than narrow the claim: touch_controls.ts now offers Fire (the space bar — alone it repeats along the facing, held with a pad direction it fires along that direction), Torch and Pause alongside the pad, Enter and the keyboard toggle, with each control on screen only where it means something so a Fire tap cannot land a space in an open text buffer. No new vocabulary reaches the simulation: every control is a key the keyboard already sends. Certified by the two Chromium touch profiles in the device matrix, which play the CONTROL world with no keyboard at all — walk, shoot both of vanilla's ways, carry a torch to the dark board and light it, pause and un-pause — each act tick-locked on the input frame the server received. The copy test stays named here because it now pins the claim from the other side: the desktop-only disclaimer it required while this row was `gap` is released by the row passing. M16.18b (2026-08-01) then took the bar off the board: it publishes its measured height and the screen letterboxes above it, so the rows it used to cover on a landscape phone are declared empty on every profile in the device matrix. M21.5 (2026-08-04) added the multiplayer controls to the same bar and the same profiles: Chat and Players open the two windows that were on letter keys a phone cannot press, Esc closes a window that Enter and the pad cannot, and a new `prompt` mode offers the Yes and No a SidebarPromptYesNo answers to — all four certified by tap on the two Chromium touch profiles, which is what the acts `windows` and `prompt` in the observation are.

rows.subject: CP437 debug window
rows.notes: M16.9: captured from the real client canvas in headless Chromium (cell goldens decoded from the canvas backing store, not from Go's PNG renderer) against the production server objects with the tick loop under test control. GameDebugPrompt's bare 11-wide sidebar field, opened with '?'.

rows.subject: Dream-a-world prompt/progress window
rows.notes: M16.17: a real browser walked the flow — D on the title screen, the premise window (its title, its 'Enter: dream' affordance and the typed premise), the 'Dreaming a world' progress window rendering the server's stages as sentences clamped to the window's 42 columns, then the dreamed world's title screen and the world itself joined and played. Every stage generation.go can emit is scanned out of the code and required to have copy in web/src/dream.ts, so a new stage cannot reach the window as a raw token. The gap it left — no repaint offer for a salvaged world — LANDED as M16.17c 2026-07-31: pollDreamJob carries a complete job's retryable/stubbedBoards out as a DreamResult instead of dropping them, and the client enters the world and then offers 'Some rooms would not form' naming the lost rooms, whose repaint resumes the same job id (M12.22's retryDreamBoard). The browser journey now takes the offer and plays the room the repaint gave back. The offer is made at the world's title screen, BEFORE the player joins, because a repaint rewrites the world's file and the server refuses to overwrite a world anybody is playing (M16.17b) — a player who took it from inside the stub room would be the occupant blocking it.

rows.notes: M16.15: a signed-in player's state reaches saves/chat.jsonl.playerstate.json on every drop and beside the .SAV on every manual save; a guest never appears in either. The inventory returns on a fresh join after a process restart and after the reconnect grace has expired, while the run itself (PlayerID, stat, position) does not (DEVIATION account-sidecar-restore). -fresh resets the world, not the accounts.

rows.notes: M16.16: the whole OIDC round trip on the production routes against a hermetic provider that checks PKCE; guest vs signed-in join identity; the callback refusal matrix and the forged-cookie matrix, each proving no session and no state change; a guest-only server; and a real browser signing in with G

rows.subject: Chat filtering / rate-limit / history
rows.notes: M16.16a: 120-byte printable-CP437 normalization, 5-per-10s rolling limit on the injected clock, refusals persist/broadcast nothing, history survives restart; M16.16: a line is attributed to the signed-in account's display name (not the name the client claimed) on the wire, in the persisted record, in the history a restarted server replays, and on a real browser's screen M21.1: a chat line now carries the sender's PlayerID, and BroadcastGlobalChat drops it for any recipient who has blocked that sender — per-recipient, silent, and covering the fifty-line history replay too. The sender's accountID is persisted on the ChatRecord (so a durable block still filters the backlog after a restart) and is never on the wire.

rows.subject: Dream plan→paint→repair generation + host/join
rows.notes: M16.17 drove the whole service through the shipped binary against a scripted model: a premise became a plan, boards, a salvaged stub, a retry-in-place that repainted it, a validated world persisted with its three sidecars into the production hosting directory, listed by the picker as a dream and joined and played over a real WebSocket — while a room already being played went on ticking and its recording replayed to the same per-tick StateHash it had put on the wire. Also certified: ZWD.md's limits table refused with a named reason, the decompile/recompile fixed point and the vanilla-reader gate on generated bytes, adversarial model output (no plan, no board, an upstream 500, a 2MB answer, a traversal world name) leaving no file and no instance, and the concurrency semaphore admitting only MaxConcurrent. THREE DEFECTS FOUND, all filed and pinned: M16.17a — every ZWD compile rewrote the process-global ElementDefs, so two dreams at once (the shipped ZZT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY=2) made each other fail with a nonsense 'unknown element name' or panic on a torn string in an unrecovered goroutine, and the table is the one every live room reads each tick — LANDED 2026-07-31: the table is built once at boot (ensureElementDefs) and the ZWD compile, decompile, blueprint and generation paths read it instead of rebuilding it, the pin is inverted, and the journey now runs the production concurrency of 2; M16.17b — a generation persisted before it hosted, so one aimed at a world people are playing replaced that world's file and its sidecars and only then reported 'already occupied' — LANDED 2026-07-31: refuseIfOccupied asks the editor's question at the editor's moment, once as soon as the name is known (so an occupied name costs no model spend) and again immediately before the first write, the route answers 409, and the pin is inverted — a refused dream now moves no byte and writes no sidecar; M16.17c — a salvaged job is complete+retryable with stubbedBoards and no client read either field, so M12.22's targeted repaint was unreachable from a browser — LANDED 2026-07-31: the client carries a complete job's salvage state out of pollDreamJob, enters the world and offers the repaint of the rooms the dream lost, and the browser journey takes the offer and plays the repainted room (carried by the mode.modal-dream row, now pass). DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED by M16.17b: generation still ignores the .access.json ownership the editor writes, so an UNOCCUPIED world of a name a tester supplies is still replaced — an owner decision, recorded in NOTES.md 2026-07-31. M16.17d and M18.11 LANDED 2026-08-01, together, because the second needs the first: the canonical Museum worlds (worlds.manifest.json, the population the picker calls `classic`) are now refused to every player-authored write — a dream and an editor publish both — which M16.17b's ownership guard could not do for them, since they carry no .access.json and read to it as unowned and open. The Museum's own cache is deliberately NOT gated: writing a classic's canonical bytes into the hosting directory is that cache doing its job, and a boundary test pins it. And because the browser sends no name, a dream's name comes from the plan: a plan-derived name that hits a classic or another account's world now falls back to the minted GEN%05X name and says so in the progress window, while a name the player TYPED still refuses with 409. A workstation audit of 65 canonical worlds found none carrying a dream or publish sidecar; the dev and production hosts need the same check, owner-gated.

rows.subject: Collaborative editor leases/presence/publish
rows.notes: M16.14 drove the whole collaborative contract through three real browsers — two accounts signed in through a hermetic OIDC provider plus a guest — on one session: live diffs and cursors, a local echo caught while the session's own lock was held, stale inspect replies dropped, per-board and per-stat leases with named refusals, release on an abrupt disconnect, ownership/invite/read-only refusal with the world's bytes unchanged, simultaneous same-cell edits converging, the publish occupancy refusal, and co-op test play in one isolated instance. It found three divergences and M16.14a closed them: (a) Clear board, Board Information, Add board, Import board and New world now fan out — the members watching the affected board get the frame, and everyone else the world-scoped half (the switcher's board list and the world name) with no frame that would paint another board over theirs, the client taking only what a snapshot addressed to somebody else is entitled to change; (b) an invite sends the invitee a snapshot addressed to them, carrying the cursor they last reported, so their browser stops refusing their own edits without re-entering; (c) a stat lease key resolves against the board that was asked for, like the board lease always did, so a collaborator's board switch can no longer strand a lease under the shared engine. M16.14a then found the one thing left, and M16.14b (2026-08-01) closed it: the diff fan-out happened outside the session's lock, so two members writing the same cell at once could have their two diffs reach a third browser in the opposite order, leaving that screen holding the tile the session threw away until something asked for a repaint. Every edit now takes a fan-out ticket in the same critical section that wrote the tile and broadcasts through the session's ordering gate, which holds no session lock while it writes, so a fan-out can block no edit, lease, inspect or entry snapshot. TestM1614bContestedCellSettlesTheSameOnEveryScreen forces the wrong order rather than waiting for load to supply it: a hook holds the first fan-out inside the gate with its tile already written, the second edit is sent while it is held, and the third member's socket must stay silent until the gate lets the first go — after which all three screens and the session's own frame end on one tile. M16.14e (2026-08-02) closed the last of them, found by M16.20's clean-clone run and pre-existing since long before the gate: every message carried a one-second write deadline, and the WebSocket library closes a connection whose write deadline expires, so a collaborator whose browser was busy for one second lost its editor socket and its client drew the title screen of the world it was editing. Each client now has a bounded outbound queue drained by its own writer goroutine, so a broadcast hands over a message instead of waiting on a browser: a stalled member costs itself latency and costs the session nothing, and is handed everything it missed, in order, when it reads again. A client that has not read 256 messages is disconnected deliberately and logged (owner decision 2026-08-02) rather than dropping messages onto a screen that would then be wrong. Both M16.14e tests force the stall — the reader's kernel buffer is shrunk and it stops reading — and refuse to pass unless the socket really blocked.

rows.subject: Solo editor + portable .ZZT/.BRD export
rows.notes: M16.13: a browser authors a world from nothing, downloads it as .ZZT and one board as .BRD, and the bytes are read back by an independent vanilla-format reader (m1613ReadVanillaWorld) and compared field by field with the editor session. The .BRD is byte-identical to that board's record inside the .ZZT, the download re-uploads through the validation gate byte for byte, and test play leaves the editing world byte-identical. M18.11: the publish path also refuses a canonical Museum world by name, before the ownership question it already asked — the classics have no .access.json for that question to read. A world the manifest does not know publishes exactly as it did.

rows.subject: Per-world high-score list entry/display
rows.notes: M16.15: a death (#endgame, routed through the respawn path) offers no slot and writes no <WORLD>.HI at all; a confirmed quit at the same score produces highScoreEntry at list position 1, and the name submitted for it is persisted to <WORLD>.HI (DEVIATION score-on-quit).

rows.subject: Museum search/select/host/join
rows.notes: M16.16a: caching is a post-validation commit; every refusal creates no cache entry, hosted .ZZT, or instance; M16.16: the same contracts through /api/museum/*, plus search dedup/not-found/upstream failure and a real browser completing search -> select -> host -> join

rows.subject: GameDebugPrompt / PromptString: the '?' 11-wide debug command field, applied via GameApplyDebugCommand
rows.notes: Typing AMMO then ENTER is compared two ways: the typed text appears in the oracle's sidebar field (PARITY.md oracle-sidebar-prompt-line normalization) before submission, and the Ammo counter's +5 effect (GameApplyDebugCommand) is compared as an ordinary counter afterward — the field's rendering and the command's real effect both verified.

rows.subject: 'H' help window: TextWindowDisplayFile('GAME.HLP', 'Playing ZZT')
rows.notes: The engine's HelpEvent carries only a filename/title (M3.9); the adapter loads GAME.HLP itself via TextWindowOpenFile, the function the interactive path also calls, and compares its first page against the oracle's window (PARITY.md oracle-modal-scroll normalization). GAME.HLP's '$Getting Started.' heading line surfaced a real gap in oracleWindowCaption, which stripped only '!label;' captions — generalized to also strip a '$' heading and a ':label;' line per TXTWIND.PAS TextWindowDrawLine. The title screen's high-score LIST view (Engine.HighScoresDisplay) has no scenario here: it is drawn only by the terminal-only GameTitleLoop (engine/zzt.go), never by GameStepWithInputs or the protocol — confirmed by grep, see TestOracleParityPromptScenario's doc comment and NOTES.md. Its actually-reachable surfaces are already tracked separately: mode.modal-highscore (M16.9), input.title-highscores (M16.11), service.high-scores (M16.15).

rows.subject: GamePromptEndPlay / SidebarPromptYesNo: the 'Q'/Escape "End this game?" yes/no prompt
rows.notes: Oracle-verified via the sidebar-prompt-line normalization (PARITY.md oracle-sidebar-prompt-line): the real ZZT's fixed "End this game? " line at (63,5) is asserted against the capture text, since the headless engine only emits QuitPromptEvent and draws nothing there itself. Declining with N is proven a no-op (SubmitQuitReply(false), matching its own doc comment) by a follow-up move that still succeeds with unchanged counters. Confirming with Y (GamePlayExitRequested/QuitEvent) is not re-verified here — that effect is unit-tested elsewhere, and the vanilla return-to-title screen it triggers is already oracle-certified as the boot/title checkpoint every M16.3-M16.7 scenario shares.

rows.subject: Reconnect within/after grace; competing resume
rows.notes: M16.15: through the production binary — a dropped socket resumed inside the grace window reclaims the same PlayerID, stat, square and inventory, and a second connection presenting the same token takes the run over while the server closes the displaced socket (newest-wins). Grace EXPIRY is 545 ticks of wall clock, so it is driven tick-by-tick in-process: the stat, the token and the reclaimable position are all gone, and the stale token falls through to a fresh join.

rows.subject: Room snapshot save + rejoinable restore
rows.notes: M16.15: a manual save through the wire (S -> savePrompt -> saveFilename -> saveResult) writes SAVE01.SAV atomically; it unions the flag set on the far board, drops every player tile from both boards, and carries the saver's inventory in the vanilla one-player World.Info fields. A joiner into the restored world arrives fresh at the start square (DEVIATION snapshot-player-drop). The saved bytes are byte-identical to the world an independent replay of the same session produces at the same tick.

rows.subject: Session recording + deterministic replay
rows.notes: M16.15: for an unauthenticated or first-visit session the recording is exact — every (tick, StateHash) fingerprint the wire carried to four connections across two rooms, through a passage transfer, a drop, a resume and a quit, is reproduced in order by a replay, and the .SAV bytes match the replayed world at the save tick. M16.15a closed the one stimulus that was missing: RoomManager.ApplyPlayerState — the account-sidecar inventory a returning signed-in player is joined with — now records a "state" op, so a session containing a returning account replays to the same inventory and the same per-room StateHash instead of diverging from the first tick, silently (TestM1615aReturningAccountReplaysThroughTheServer signs in, earns the inventory, drops and rejoins through the real join handler). recordVersion is 2 and a v1 file is refused rather than mis-replayed (TestSessionRecordRefusesAnOlderVersion).

rows.subject: Portable .ZZT/.SAV world-file round trip; malformed/truncated input is refused everywhere untrusted bytes reach the loader, never panics
rows.notes: BoardOpen/worldReadFrom had no bounds checking (RLE run count, StatCount vs MAX_STAT, board count vs MAX_BOARD); LoadWorldBytes/LoadPristineWorld/RoomManager.LoadWorld/RestoreSnapshot and WorldLoad now validate every board once (validateWorldBoards, game.go) before it can reach a real BoardOpen, closing a live-server-crash gap on the multiplayer upload/host/restore path. .SAV is the same GameWorldSave routine as .ZZT (game.go) with darkness/torch/time state proven round-tripped. .BRD export/import + malformed-input refusal (editor_session_test.go, safeBoardOpen) predate this task and are exercised by service.editor-solo (M16.13); board re-entry/entry-point (elem.board-edge, M16.3) and title-screen animation (elem.monitor, M16.3) were already oracle-certified and only gained one strengthened return-trip checkpoint here (pass.scn).

rows.notes: M16.16: /api/worlds lists a Museum-imported world with its metadata and live occupancy, and a real browser reaches it through the picker window

deviations.title: Death is a respawn (penalty + brief invulnerability), not game-over
Overlapping players: the arriver is pushed to a free adjacent square
Multiplayer projectile/contact damage follows an explicit friendly-fire policy
Modals freeze only the acting player; the room keeps ticking
World.Info.Flags are shared across players (co-op puzzle progress)
A restored snapshot drops other players; a joiner arrives fresh
Per-player keys/inventory live in an account sidecar, not the snapshot
The menu omits vanilla's S game-speed — the server owns the tick
A high score is entered on quit, not on death
Movement is arrows + numpad 8/4/6/2 only; WASD removed (S collides with save)
Pickup/shot/damage sounds are per-acting-player; #play stays room-wide
A windowed scroll is consumed on reply, not on touch (de-modal)
Presentation-only additions with no vanilla counterpart (name popup, picker, overlay, chat, sound UI, Dream, help/debug windows)
Mobile ships text entry only; touch gameplay is a filed gap task (M16.18a)
